entry.title: SCIM3 PATCH API returning 403 Forbidden in SAP Analytics Cloud (GET works, Admin access available)
entry.content:
Hi folks,

I am facing an issue while using the SCIM3 API in SAP Analytics Cloud to update team members using PATCH operation.

API Details

Endpoint:

PATCH  /api/v1/scim3/Groups/<TEAM_UUID>

Authentication:
  • Authorization Bearer Token
Headers Used

  • Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

  • x-csrf-token: <csrf_token>

  • x-sap-sac-custom-auth: true

Payload
"schemas": [
            "urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"
        ],
        "Operations": [
            {
                "op":"add",
                "path":"members",
                "value":[
                    {
                        "value":"d0bbac78-776890-9876hjmd",
                        "type":"User",
                        "display":"newuser",
                        "$ref":"/api/v1/scim3/Users/d0bbac78-776890-9876hjmd"
                    }
                ]
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
            "path": "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:sap:2.0:Group:description",
            "value": "patch test"
            }
        ]
Issue

The PATCH request consistently returns:

{
"status": 403,
"error":"Forbidden"
}

Observations

  • GET operations on /api/v1/scim3/Groups are working successfully.
  • Team UUID is retrieved correctly.
  • Team type is userGroup.
  • I have full admin access (BI_Admin role) in SAP Analytics Cloud.
  • OAuth Client is configured with API access with App Integration.
  • CSRF Token is fetched and passed correctly.
  • when CSRF token is removed, the API returns 401 Unauthorized.
  • PATCH always returns 403 Forbidden.
Questions
  1. Are there additional permissions required specifically for SCIM3 PATCH operations ?
  2. Does the OAuth client require explicit SCIM provisioning(write) permissions?
  3. Are there any tenant-level restrictions for SCIM3 write operations ?
Attachments
  • PATCH request (headers + payload)

 

  • Response (403 Forbidden)

Any guidance would be helpful

Thanks!

entry.title: SAC IFP Business Content - Model import fails - parent folder missing from package
entry.content:
Issue:
When importing the SAP Business Content package "Integrated Financial Planning for SAP S/4HANA" in SAP Analytics Cloud, the object SAP_FI_IFP_IM_Profitability fails to import with the error "Parent resource does not exist."

Additional Analysis (from import screenshot):

Based on the import summary screenshot, the error is thrown specifically at the model level, not at the story or data action level. This suggests that the package itself does not include the parent folder/model structure — only the content objects that depend on it.

My assumption is that the content package was exported or packaged without including the parent folder and its associated model, which means the import process cannot resolve the dependency at runtime. The missing folder/model is a prerequisite that should have been bundled in the package from the start.

Could you confirm whether the parent folder and model are intentionally excluded from this package version, or if this is an unintended packaging issue?

 

 

 

SAP Analytics Cloud tenant: Trial

Content Package: Integrated Financial Planning for SAP S/4HANA
Content Version: IFP 1.14.0

SAP Analytics Cloud, connectivity SAP Analytics Cloud, augmented analytics SAP Analytics Cloud, data modeling

entry.title: SAC Planning – Cash Calculation Across Planning Models
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

We are implementing SAC Planning for a retail customer whose requirement is for cash in the Balance Sheet to reflect planning activities across Sales, OPEX, and CAPEX.

For example, sales are assumed to be cash sales. In OPEX, an expense incurred in January is recognized in the P&L and creates an accrued liability, while the cash payment occurs in February based on DPO assumptions. Similarly, CAPEX planning should reflect the timing of asset payments and their impact on cash.

I reviewed the standard business content and noticed that cash is calculated through the Cash Flow and then reflected in the Balance Sheet.

Should we follow this standard approach, or does the customer's requirement to reflect cash impacts directly from each planning model introduce duplicate calculations and unnecessary complexity? How should we design this to ensure accurate cash movements without double counting across the P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow?

Thank you.

 

 

 @achab @XiwenLiao  SAP Analytics Cloud for planning
